summary: Registers the input string in a fixed-capacity (32 entries x 132 bytes) most-recent-first string registry. Copies the input into a 256-byte stack buffer, preprocesses it via sub_589901, then scans the existing entries of byte_8B5A3C with strcmp. If a duplicate is found it returns without inserting. Otherwise, when entries exist, every entry is shifted up one 132-byte slot (copied with ArithmeticComparison_c6b0, indexed through dword_8B5A38), the new string is written into slot 0 of byte_8B5A3C and the global count dword_8B8E30 is incremented.

local_names.SrcStr: 256-byte stack buffer holding the copied input
local_names.v4: scan index over existing registry entries
local_names.v5: cursor into byte_8B5A3C advancing by 132 bytes per entry during the dedupe scan
local_names.v6: dword-indexed cursor into dword_8B5A38 (stride 33 dwords) during the shift loop
local_names.result: return value: 0 on duplicate, terminating index + 1 after a copy

operations.description: Registration proceeds only when the input's first byte is non-null (non-empty string) and the registry count dword_8B8E30 is below 32
Copy the input string (read through this+0) into the 256-byte stack buffer SrcStr, byte by byte, until the NUL terminator
sub_589901(SrcStr) preprocesses the stack copy before it is stored in the registry
Dedupe scan: strcmp SrcStr against each 132-byte-strided entry of byte_8B5A3C; a match breaks out and skips insertion

When no duplicate is found and count > 0, shift every existing entry up one 132-byte slot by copying with ArithmeticComparison_c6b0, indexing the entries through dword_8B5A38 (dword stride 33) so slot 0 becomes free
Copy SrcStr into byte_8B5A3C starting at slot 0, byte by byte until the NUL terminator
Registry count dword_8B8E30 is set to count + 1
Returns 0 when the string was already present, or the copy's terminating index + 1 after a successful insert
Used by pit-crew/animation setup, SpecialFX_Init, VidMan_Init and StringCompareCopy paths as a shared string registry

clean_pseudocode: copy a1 into SrcStr until NUL;
copy SrcStr into byte_8B5A3C until NUL;
unresolved: What sub_589901 does to SrcStr (normalization, lowercasing, trimming) is unknown.
The differing return values (0 on duplicate vs terminating index + 1 on insert) have unclear consumer semantics.
Why the registry keeps the newest entry at slot 0 (MRU-front ordering) and who reads the entries is unknown.
The structural relation between dword_8B5A38 (indexed in 33-dword steps) and byte_8B5A3C (132-byte slots) is consistent only arithmetically (132 = 33 * 4); the real layout is unverified.
The field this+0 is read only as the input string's first byte; no further object state is used.
